paper_title: Multiplicative Error Set System Sparsification: A Simpler Proof via Chain Length Contraction
classifications: Theory of computation → Constraint and logic programming
statement: ▶ Conjecture 23. For a set system S Ď 2rms , weights w : rms Ñ Rě0 and ϵ ą 0, there exists a p1 ˘ ϵq sparsifier of S which retains only ˆ ˙ CLpSq O ϵ2 many coordinates. Of note, even proving Conjecture 23 for linear code sparsification would be a significant result.
context: Truly linear sparsifiers. A celebrated result of Batson, Spielman and Srivastava [3] states that graphs on n vertices have p1 ˘ ϵq cut sparsifiers with Opn{ϵ2 q-edges. Furthermore, such asymptotics are known to be tight up to a constant factor [9]. Proving an analogue of [3] for arbitrary set systems seems quite difficult as there is no clear spectral analogue of set system sparsification (however, see [22]). Currently, the most general extensions of [3] are to the regime of PSD matrix sparsification in the work of [27] (which even includes arity 3 hypergraph cut sparsification). Nonetheless, we boldly conjecture that analogous constructions should exist in general. ▶ Conjecture 23. For a set system S Ď 2rms , weights w : rms Ñ Rě0 and ϵ ą 0, there exists a p1 ˘ ϵq sparsifier of S which retains only ˆ ˙ CLpSq O ϵ2 many coordinates. Of note, even proving Conjecture 23 for linear code sparsification would be a significant result.
